Interview Experience
Summer Internship 2023
AAYUSH MEHTA
TY Btech CS 2020-2024
Eligibility:
●Cgpa: 6.5 and above
●No active backlogs
●Candidate must be in their pre-final year
Stipend : INR 30,000/-
Location : Mumbai/Bengaluru/Gurgaon/Chennai
Timeline:
●PPT: 14 September
●Online Assessment: 27 September
●Technical Round: 30 September

●HR Round: 30 September
PPT:
I was unable to join the ppt due to some joining issues, but got to know that
it was the case with most of the students. Fortunately, they provided a
recorded session for us. The ppt was an hour long and covered most of the
points about the company.
Online Assessment:
The online assessment was a test of 70 questions, with a time duration of
75 minutes. The time for the test was not sufficient, so you have to be fast.
The questions overall were easy to moderate.
The assessment consisted of 4 phases:
1. Data Analysis: In this round, all the questions were graphical
and statistical. Basic knowledge of statistics should be more
than sufficient. There were some tricky questions. You need to
be familiar with charts.
2. Reasoning Ability: Some logical reasoning questions were
asked. The questions were easy but time consuming. Make
sure you don’t waste a lot of time stuck on a single question.

3. Quantitative Ability: Logical mathematics questions. Since you
guys cleared JEE/CET, this section won’t be much of a
challenge. Be fast and read the questions properly and you’ll be
fine.
4. Verbal Ability: This section was the most challenging for me as
I had very little time left, about less than 10 minutes. I randomly
selected most of the answers. The level of difficulty was
moderate to difficult.
Advice :   Pretend that you’re writing CET. Be fast and sharp. 204
candidates had given the test out of which 23 candidates were
selected. From talking with the other candidates selected, I can
conclude that data analysis was the most important section and
might have been the deciding factor followed by the other sections.
So keep your cool while writing the test and be really fast.
Technical Round:
So, I was the first one in the interview schedule. Everyone was allotted 15
minutes. My allotted time was 9am - 9:15am.
(Tip: Always join 15 minutes before the allotted time)
I had joined 15 minutes before, and fortunately for me, my interviewer
also joined 10 minutes before the allotted time. So we started the interview
early as there was already less time. So by joining early, I extended the

interview from 15 minutes to 25/30 minutes.
So, the first question, tell me about yourself. Always be prepared for this
question. Since the interview was short, I kept the answer short and upto to
the point. Then she asked about my projects. I gave an overview about
them. One of my projects was related to text summarization and she had
knowledge about that so she asked me more questions related to it and
libraries used. She asked me the difference when I used pegasus and bart.
Then she asked me which language I was familiar with. I told her
python, as the company used it. Always familiarize which language is
needed by the company. She asked me basic questions about python. Tell
me the data structures used in python but not in other languages. I told her
tuples, sets, and dictionaries. Then she went on to ask about dictionaries
and was later told to write a simple code in python to print fibonacci
sequence. I had mentioned two certification courses in my CV. So she
asked me what I learned in the course. The courses were on data analysis
and data science. Then she asked me about my familiarity with SQL. She
asked me many questions based on sql. Some that I remember are-Tell me
all the joins you know. What are cartesian joins, self joins? How do you
identify if there is null in the table? Some basic sql queries. Then she asked
me if I knew what a data frame was in pandas.
At the end, when time was up, she asked me a hypothetical question:
if you couldn’t complete a task assigned to you in time, what would you tell
your boss? She asked another HR question about how you would proceed,
if in your team, you and another team member had a conflict of interest in
the decision that would change your project.

Advice : To be honest, this was one of the easiest technical interviews
I had been in. So be confident and always smile. If you ever come up
without any immediate answers, always try to ask counter questions.
If even that’s not coming to mind, never hesitate to say you don’t
know the answer. Being quiet is far worse than being wrong. Keep the
interview interactive. Do not lie on your resume, even if you do, make
sure you know all the stuff about the specified technology or the
project. Most of the questions will be asked based on your resume.
Make your resume easy to read and add links to all the projects and
certifications. When explaining your project, don’t use over-simplified
terms. Explain it as if you are explaining to a professional. There is no
need to hurry in any answer, be calm and yourself and you’ll start
enjoying the interview.
HR Round:
30 minutes after giving the technical round, I received an email
regarding the HR round. It was scheduled for 9:30-9:45am. Again 15
minutes. This time again, I joined 10 minutes early. The interviewer joined
the meeting at 9:30. The first question, of course, tell me about yourself. I
again repeated the same things as mentioned in the technical interview, but
added some soft skills as well. The second question being, what do you
know about Fractal. I flustered a little, now knowing much, but I tried to tell

whatever I knew. I should’ve gone with more knowledge about the company
and points from the ppt, my biggest mistake of the interview. Thankfully, the
interviewer didn’t seem to mind much about it. He even corrected me
regarding some of the points. So, after that was over, he asked me whether
I had worked with a team before. I told him about my hackathon
experiences, and he seemed to be impressed. Then he told me that he
would ask me a logical question, he asked me this question. I came up with
the answer pretty quickly. He was pretty impressed with it. He asked
another logical question, being this. I worked out in the notebook and gave
the answer. So after that was over, he asked me basic HR questions. How
will you work under deadline pressure? What will you do if a colleague asks
about a project whose technology you are not familiar with? Then we talked
about a few things about work culture. And that was pretty much it. In the
end, he asked if I had any questions. Never say no to this question. Come
up with something. I asked a question and then the interview was over.
Advice : Be confident while speaking, keep a smile on your face and talk as
if you’re talking to a colleague. Prepare for standard HR questions. Read
about the company and its feats and achievements. If you have the ppt
recording, watch it before the HR round. Always ask a question at the end,
be it about the job profile, the work culture, or any other advice which you
can take from the interviewer. That’s it. Just be yourself and you’ll surely
pass the interview. All the best :)
